we have prepared a new type of Brønsted acid-base 2ILs that are stable up to 200 degrees C and have a high conductivity, and that we have incorporated them into polymeric membranes that are stable up the same temperature and have an ionic conductivity in the same range.
a series of new IL-based, proton conducting membranes are prepared and tested as new polymer electrolyte for high-temperature PEMFCs.

a novel type of Brønsted acid-base 2,6-dimethylpyridine-based ILs are prepared and incorporated in a poly(vinfluenidene-co-hexafluropropylene) matrix to produce membranes with a high ionic conduction and a high decomposition temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterizations of new types of ionic liquids-based polymer electrolytes for fuel cell applications.
the synthesis and characterization of new ILs, and with their use in the fabrication of novel proton-conducting membrane materials for applications in PEM fuel cells.
the preparation of new ILs with a high melting point and high ionic conductivity.

a series of IL-based membranes are proposed as novel polymer electrolytes for applications in PEMCs.
the IL-based membranes have the potential to be used in high-temperature PEMFCs.
the use of Brönsted acidic IL-based membranes in PEMFCs is a promising alternative to the current commercial Nafion membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ILs are good materials for fuel cell applications and that the ILs-based membranes have a potential to replace the current state-of-the-art Nafion membranes.

we have successfully developed and characterized a new series of Brønsted acid-base 2:1 type ionic liquids and their membranes, which can be used in the high-temperature PEMFCs as a new type of proton-conducting electrolyte.

the new types of Brönsteds acid-base ionic liquid-based polymer membranes have been developed and the membranes are proposed as a new type of polymer electrolytes for applications in high-temperature PEMFCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ILs are stable up to 200 degrees C.
the use of a Brönsted acid as the anion of the ionic liquid (IL) allows the preparation of a novel type of proton conducting ILs, which are very stable at high temperatures.
the use of a Brönsted acid as an anion in ILs is a promising way to obtain new types of IL-based, proton conducting membranes with good thermal stability and a high conductivity.
